RESEARCH ONLY. No code, no .md report files. Return findings as final message text with EXACT QUOTES + URLs.

IMPORTANT CORRECTED URLS (I verified these live — do not waste time on thunderstore.io/tos/, it returns a real 404):
- https://thunderstore.io/tos/ -> 404 (does not exist)
- The footer of https://thunderstore.io/ links ONLY to: https://pages.thunderstore.io/p/privacy-policy (HTTP 200)
- https://pages.thunderstore.io/p/terms-of-service, /p/tos, /p/terms, /p/content-policy, /p/acceptable-use, /p/dmca all return 404
- https://thunderstore.io/package/create/docs/ 301-redirects to https://wiki.thunderstore.io/mods/creating-a-package

Your job — find whether a Thunderstore TERMS OF SERVICE / content policy / upload license grant exists AT ALL, and quote it:

1. Fetch https://pages.thunderstore.io/p/privacy-policy in full. Quote any section touching: user-uploaded content, licensing, third-party access, API use, data redistribution, or commercial use. Note it names subprocessors (Cloudflare, DigitalOcean, Gcore, Sentry, NitroPay, Overwolf) — quote what it says about Overwolf specifically.

2. Explore https://wiki.thunderstore.io/ thoroughly. Fetch the sitemap or index. Look for: package format spec (https://wiki.thunderstore.io/mods/creating-a-package), content/upload rules, moderation policy, API docs, rate-limit guidance, any terms. Quote the EXACT manifest.json field list from the package spec and state explicitly whether a `license` field exists. Also quote any README requirements.

3. WebSearch for: "Thunderstore terms of service", "Thunderstore content policy", "Thunderstore package license", "Thunderstore API terms of use", "thunderstore.io legal". Also check https://github.com/thunderstore-io (org README, the thunderstore/thunderstore repo, its LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, and any docs/ folder) for terms or API-use policy. Check if there is a Thunderstore Discord/blog post about API usage or mirroring.

4. Search specifically for Thunderstore's stated position on THIRD-PARTY MOD MANAGERS: r2modman (github.com/ebkr/r2modmanPlus), Gale (github.com/Kesomannen/gale), and Thunderstore's own "Thunderstore Mod Manager" / Overwolf partnership. Is there any statement blessing, tolerating, or restricting third-party clients that auto-download packages? Note that the Thunderstore API has an endpoint literally documented as "Used by Thunderstore Mod Manager" (/api/experimental/auth/overwolf/login/), and that r2modman was later acquired/absorbed by Thunderstore — verify that and cite.

5. Check whether Thunderstore has a commercial/hosting partnership: I observed a "dathost-link" CSS class and an "Ad / 30% off!" badge injected into thunderstore.io page HTML, suggesting a DatHost (game server hosting) advertising deal. Verify and cite what that relationship is. This matters because our client is a competing game-server host.

6. State CLEARLY at the end: does a binding Thunderstore ToS exist that a third party can point to? If NO formal ToS exists, say so explicitly — that is itself the key finding. Do not invent or infer text.

Answer each with a direct quote + URL, or explicitly "NOT FOUND — no such text exists at any URL I could reach".

DigitalOcean, GCore, New Relic).

 Creating a Package
 Requirements for a valid Thunderstore package
 Basics 
 This page only outlines the basic requirements of a Thunderstore package. For game and loader specific instructions, see packaging your mods. 
 A valid Thunderstore package is a zip file which must contain at least the following files at the root of the zip:
 Name
 Description
 icon.png
 PNG icon for the mod, must be 256x256 resolution.
 README.md
 Readme in markdown syntax. Will be rendered on the package's page.
 manifest.json
 JSON file with metadata of the package. See Manifest for structure.
 Packages can also contain a CHANGELOG.md 
 File naming is case-sensitive and must match the above exactly! 
 In addition to these required files, the package can include any number of additional mod-specific files.
 Currently there's a maximum package size limit of 5 242 880 000 bytes (or roughly 5 GB) , but this is a soft-limit and can be increased if needed. If you do face this scenario, contact us and request an increase.
 Example of a minimal package viewed with 7-Zip :
 Minimal Thunderstore package opened with 7-Zip 
 package-example.zip 
 archive · 53KB
 Download Open 
 Example package Icon 
 A valid icon has to be exactly 256x256 in resolution and in PNG format.
 Transparency is supported, although if used, it is recommended the icon has clear borders that work with any background color as icons might be displayed in a variety of themes (e.g. with 3rd party mod managers).
 Animated PNG files are technically valid, but only the first frame will display on some pages / embeds.
 README 
 Structure 
 The readme supports markdown syntax, closely but not exactly matching that of GitHub's. You can view GitHub markdown docs here and general markdown docs here .
 As the markdown used by Thunderstore doesn't match GitHub 100%, it is recommended the Markdown Preview tool built in to Thunderstore is used for previewing the content.
 Markdown Preview Tool Example 
 Encoding 
 The readme has to be UTF-8 compatible (use Notepad++ or VS Code to check for encoding if you aren't sure). If you're using a new enough version of Windows, you can also check the encoding while saving the file:
 Windows notepad save dialog 
 UTF-8 Is generally compatible with other encodings, as many of them share a similar structure for common characters. Generally you will only hit encoding issues if special characters are involved, in which case converting to UTF-8 should solve the issue.
 The markdown preview tool is unable to check for file encoding, as that is a property of the file save format, and the validator does not read files.
 Manifest 
 The manifest.json file is what tells Thunderstore and other tools some critical technical information about your package (such as the name & version). Some of it may also be used for presentation.
 The file should be in standard JSON format (UTF-8 encoded) with the following contents:
 Key
 Description
 name
 Name of the mod, no spaces. Allowed characters: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ 
 description
 A short description of the mod, shown on the mod list. Max 250 characters.
 version_number
 Version number of the mod, following the semantic version format Major.Minor.Patch
 dependencies
 A list of other packages that are required for this package to function. 
 website_url
 URL of the mod's website (e.g. GitHub repo). Can be left an empty string.
 You can use the Manifest Validator tool to validate your manifest before packaging it to a zip.
 Name 
 Max length of a name is 128 characters and it cannot contain characters other than abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_ .
 Underscores are replaced with a space in most views when displaying the mod name, so it's recommended they are used in place of where space normally would.
 Description 
 Short description of the package, will be displayed in list views and other views where a full length readme cannot be shown. 250 characters max.
 Version Number 
 The version number of the package, following the 3-numbered Major.Minor.Patch semantic version format.
 For example, version 1.3.2 is newer than 1.2.23 but older than 2.1.0 . Be mindful that these are not decimal numbers, and adding an extra zero at the end is significant. For example 1.0.10 is 9 patch versions higher than 1.0.1 . Each version number part is a full number.
 Thunderstore will always display the highest package version regardless of upload date
 To update a package, simply increment its version number and re-upload it.
 Dependencies 
 Dependencies declared in the manifest are automatically installed by the mod manager when a package is installed.
 The dependencies field should be a list of strings, each string being a reference to a valid Thunderstore package.
 The format used by Thunderstore to refer to other packages is as follows: {team name}-{package name}-{package version} , and you can find a Dependency string field matching this format on each package page:
 Dependency String Location 
 Example dependencies:
 Website URL 
 A website URL is optional, although an empty string is required even if no URL is included. If included, it will be added to the package page as a link.
 Full example 
 Creating the ZIP file 
 Windows 
 To create a package ZIP file on Windows, the easiest way is as follows:
 Highlight all the files you intend to pack using Windows explorer
 Tip: Use ctrl + click to select multiple files
 Right click any of the selected files
 Choose the Send to -> Compressed (zipped) folder 
 Send to zipped folder windows dialog 
 After doing the above, a zip file with a name matching one of the files should be created.
 Make sure to select individual files to create a zip of instead of the directory they're within. If you zip the directory instead, the files will not reside at the root of the zip, thus making the package invalid.
 Other 
 On other systems, any tool capable of creating standard ZIP files should suffice. Our recommended option is 7-Zip , which is available on all platforms.

 Global Rules
 Rules that apply to all communities on Thunderstore
 Below is a list of basic rules that should be enforced in every community on Thunderstore. Some communities may have more specific or stricter rules than the ones found here.
 Unlawful Content 
 Packages that contain unlawful content are not allowed. 
 Copyright and Licensing 
 Copyright laws and code licensing must be followed where applicable.
 Do not distribute game files such as Assembly-CSharp.dll, unless given explicit permission by the game's developers.
 Do not reupload packages or assets by other authors unless you have permission to redistribute them or are following their licensing.
 Malware 
 Packages containing malware are not allowed. 
 Packages that deceptively disrupt or damage other software or hardware are considered malware. This includes keyloggers, crypto miners, token stealers, and other malicious programs. These packages are still considered malware even if the author discloses that they contain such capabilities.
 A few examples of packages that are malware: 
 A package that secretly collects personal information on people who use it.
 A package called "Furry Fun Pack" that purposely crashes your game when you launch it.
 A package called "One Million Fish" that adds new fish to the game, but also bans a player named Steve from any server with the mod.
 A package called "Bananas" that adds bananas to the game, but also closes your game if you live in China.
 A few examples of packages that aren't necessarily malware: 
 A package called "Your game closes if you die" that closes your game if you die.
 A package called "Secure Server Banlist" that bans Steve and his friends from connecting to any server with the mod.
 NSFW Content 
 All packages containing NSFW content must have the "Contains NSFW content" option selected. 
 Sexually explicit content such as nudity is not allowed in the icon, README, changelog, or any other file that gets displayed on the Thunderstore website or mod manager.
 Compatibility and the Ecosystem 
 Where possible, packages should not contain obfuscated code (or execute code downloaded from external sources). Obfuscation makes it difficult to audit malicious behavior and fix incompatibilities with other packages.
 Packages should rely on external mod managers for updates, rather than be capable of updating themselves.
 Harassment and Abuse 
 Packages made with the intent to harm a group, platform, or individual are not allowed. 
 This includes (but is not limited to):
 Doxxing.
 Hate speech.
 Denial of service attacks.
 Spam 
 Packages that could be considered spam are not allowed. 
 This includes (but is not limited to):
 Packages that don't do anything.
 Packages that are an exact reupload of an existing package.
 Packages that exist primarily to advertise an outside platform or service.
 Low effort packages that could otherwise be a single package (the same author uploading x2 money, x3 money, x4 money, etc. instead of a single Money Multiplier mod).
 Untested or non-functional AI-generated mods.
 Misconfigured packages or packages with incorrect / misleading titles, descriptions, and icons may also be removed.
 AI Generated Content 
 A package with AI generated assets or code should be given the AI Generated category if such a category exists in the community the package was uploaded to. This is generally not enforced for README's or icons.
 Packages should be tested before upload, and have READMEs that accurate describe their current functionality.

[![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/github/license/ebkr/r2modmanPlus?color=orange&style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/ebkr/r2modmanPlus)

| [Features](#features) | [What is a mod manager?](#what-is-a-mod-manager) | [Installing](#installing) | [Help](#help) | [Feedback and suggestions](#feedback-and-suggestions) | [Changelog](#changelog) | [Screenshots](#screenshots) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Features
- Support for Risk of Rain 2, Dyson Sphere Program, Valheim, GTFO, BONEWORKS, and more
- A clean user interface designed to make modding as simple as possible
- Safer mod installation allowing you to play the game through Steam normally
- Mod profiles to switch between different sets of mods quickly and easily
- Export profiles to easily share both your mods and configs with friends
- Download and install mods directly from the manager
- View and update any outdated mods
- Edit configs directly from the manager
- Auto-updates
- And more!

## What is a mod manager?
It's quite simple really, a mod manager is an application to make it easier to control which mods you have installed.

You can choose to update, enable/disable or even uninstall mods with a simple click, all whilst keeping it available on another profile.

## Installing

### Windows
1. Click "Manual Download" on Thunderstore.
2. Inside the downloaded **.zip** file. Run the "r2modman Setup X.X.X.exe" (where X.X.X is the current version).
3. Follow the steps in the installer.

### Linux

If you are on Linux, please do not install the `.exe` files of r2modman. Instead, use one of the following methods:

#### Steam Deck

The Steam Deck relies on Flatpak installations if you'd like to use r2modman in game mode.

If you prefer to run the manager in desktop mode, you can use either the Flatpak (recommended) or the AppImage.

#### Flatpak and AppImage

1. Click "Manual Download" on Thunderstore.
2. Extract the downloaded **.zip** file.
2. Inside the extracted folder, there will be:
  - A `flatpak-setup.sh` file. Run this script if you want to install r2modman via Flatpak. (Recommended).
  - An AppImage file for regular usage. This file may need to be marked as executable (`chmod +x <filename>.AppImage`).

The `flatpak-setup.sh` script consists of:
```bash
flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists r2builds https://r2builds.ebkr.dev/flatpak/r2modman.flatpakrepo
flatpak install -y r2builds io.github.ebkr.r2modman
```

You will need elevated privileges (sudo) to run the `flatpak-setup.sh` script or the commands as listed above.

If you'd prefer not to use sudo/elevated privileges to install the Flatpak, then you can run the following manually:
```bash
flatpak remote-add --user --if-not-exists r2builds http://r2builds.ebkr.dev/flatpak/r2modman.flatpakrepo
flatpak install --user io.github.ebkr.r2modman
```

#### Platform-specific builds

_If you'd prefer to install platform specific builds then you can find them under the latest GitHub release on the ebkr/r2modmanPlus repository_

Platform builds:
 - deb
 - rpm

# Thunderstore

[![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/thunderstore-io/Thunderstore/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/thunderstore-io/Thunderstore)

Thunderstore is a mod database and API for downloading mods. This repository holds
the **Django backend**, the REST API, and the legacy
web UI. The new web frontend lives in a separate repository,
[thunderstore-ui](https://github.com/thunderstore-io/thunderstore-ui).

## Contents

-   [Getting started](#getting-started)
-   [How the dev environment works](#how-the-dev-environment-works)
-   [Running the frontend](#running-the-frontend)
-   [Everyday tasks](#everyday-tasks)
-   [Testing](#testing)
-   [Production configuration](#production-configuration)
-   [License](#license)

## Getting started

You need [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) with Docker Compose.

1. **Configure the environment.** Copy the template and adjust if needed:

    ```bash
    cp .env.template .env
    ```

    If you have the `python-packages` submodule cloned and want its extras, set
    `BUILD_INSTALL_EXTRAS=true` (only the literal value `true` works). Changing it
    later requires a rebuild with `docker compose build`.

2. **Start the backend:**

    ```bash
    docker compose up -d
    ```

3. **Seed the database.** This runs migrations, populates test data, creates the
   site mappings, and creates a default `admin` / `admin` superuser:

    ```bash
    docker compose exec django python manage.py setup_dev_env
    ```

    > **Existing database?** Re-run `setup_dev_env` after pulling a change to
    > the dev domains: it resets the `Site` and `CommunitySite` mappings to the
    > `*.localhost` domains described below (pass `--skip-test-data` to keep
    > your existing data). A database from an older setup lacks these mappings,
    > which surfaces as broken community pages on the legacy site — re-running
    > the command replaces any manual Django-admin cleanup.

The backend is now ready. You can open:

-   **Legacy site** — <http://old.thunderstore.localhost> (works with just the backend)
-   **Admin panel** — <http://thunderstore.localhost/djangoadmin/> (log in with `admin` / `admin`)
-   **Main site** — <http://thunderstore.localhost> (needs the frontend running, see
    [Running the frontend](#running-the-frontend))

Run `docker compose logs -f` to follow the logs.

## How the dev environment works

nginx listens on **port 80** and is the single entry point. It routes by hostname:

-   **`thunderstore.localhost`** — the new main site (Cyberstorm Remix, codenamed
    Nimbus). nginx proxies app routes to the Remix dev server and serves Django's
    `/api`, `/auth`, `/djangoadmin`, `/media`, `/static`, … on the **same origin**,
    so server-side rendering and the browser share one API origin.

Writing up the findings. ## BOTTOM LINE (answering #6 first) **NO binding, published Thunderstore Terms of Service exists that a third party can point to.** This is the key finding, and it is not an inference — it is confirmed four independent ways: 1. Every plausible URL 404s (list below). 2. Neither the new site's nor the legacy site's footer links to one — only Contact Us + Privacy Policy. 3. `grep -rn -i "terms of service"` across a full clone of the backend (`thunderstore-io/Thunderstore`, AGPL-3.0) returns **zero hits**. So does `"you agree"` / `"agree to"`. 4. Thunderstore's **own frontend code contains a `TermsOfService` link that points at a page that does not exist** (see #6 detail below). --- ## 1. Privacy Policy — https://pages.thunderstore.io/p/privacy-policy (HTTP 200) Data controller: **"The data controller for the processing described in this notice is: Riskidev Oy"** (Finnish company). Legal contact: `legal@thunderstore.io`. **On user-uploaded content** — there is NO license grant, NO redistribution term, NO commercial-use term. The only references to uploaded content are as *personal-data categories*: > "Thunderstore is primarily interested in collecting data which directly enables functionality of the platform (such as mod uploads or login details)." > "(C) **Usage Data** include information about how you use and interact with our website, e.g., your downloads on our website and content you create to our website." > "To access and manage the content you post on our website, including removing illegal, harmful and abusive content. | (C) Usage | Processing is necessary for our legitimate interest to provide you a safe service and **to abide by our Terms of Services**." **That last clause is the single most important sentence in the whole document for your purposes.** The privacy policy asserts that a "Terms of Services" exists — but it is nowhere published, nowhere linked, and nowhere in the open-source codebase. A document referenced-but-never-published cannot be enforced against a third party who was never given notice of it. **On third-party access / API use / data redistribution:** NOT FOUND — no such text exists in the privacy policy. It covers only GDPR processing of personal data. **On Overwolf specifically** (two mentions): > "(A) **Identity and Contact Data** includes your username, email and possible other data associated with our Authentication Providers (e.g. Discord, GitHub or **Overwolf**)" > "Advertising providers NitroPay and **Overwolf** also use our website or desktop application to collect information on you through cookies. We do not directly provide this information to them, but we allow them to access the data on our website for ad setting purposes. ... https://www.overwolf.com/legal/privacy/ (Overwolf)." And from the summary section: > "...by allowing our ad vendors to embed ads on the platform (**NitroPay, Overwolf**) or routing our traffic through them (Cloudflare, DigitalOcean, GCore, **New Relic**)." Minor inconsistency worth noting: the summary names **New Relic**, but section 4's actual disclosure list names only Sentry.io, Cloudflare, GCore and DigitalOcean — New Relic never reappears. Sentry is disclosed as: *"Sentry.io (https://sentry.io/privacy/) provides us an error logging system."* ## 2. The wiki — https://wiki.thunderstore.io/ The **entire wiki is 15 pages** (confirmed via `sitemap-pages.xml` and `llms.txt`). There is **no terms page, no API page, no rate-limit page, no licensing page.** **Exact manifest.json field list** from https://wiki.thunderstore.io/mods/creating-a-package: | Key | Description | |---|---| | `name` | "Name of the mod, no spaces. Allowed characters: a-z A-Z 0-9 _" | | `description` | "A short description of the mod, shown on the mod list. Max 250 characters." | | `version_number` | "Version number of the mod, following the semantic version format Major.Minor.Patch" | | `dependencies` | "A list of other packages that are required for this package to function." | | `website_url` | "URL of the mod's website (e.g. GitHub repo). Can be left an empty string." | **There is NO `license` field. Explicitly confirmed at the code level** — `django/thunderstore/repository/package_manifest.py:47` `class ManifestV1Serializer` declares exactly: `name`, `version_number`, `website_url`, `description`, `dependencies`, plus an undocumented optional `installers`. And `grep -rn -i "license" django/thunderstore/repository/*.py` returns **zero** non-test hits. **Thunderstore does not capture, require, or store a license for any uploaded package.** **README requirements:** > "README.md — Readme in markdown syntax. Will be rendered on the package's page." > "File naming is case-sensitive and must match the above exactly!" > "The readme has to be UTF-8 compatible" > "The readme supports markdown syntax, closely but not exactly matching that of GitHub's." Package size cap: **"Currently there's a maximum package size limit of 5 242 880 000 bytes (or roughly 5 GB), but this is a soft-limit and can be increased if needed."** **The closest thing to content rules** is https://wiki.thunderstore.io/moderation/global-rules — note this is *moderation guidance for moderators*, not a user contract: > "**Copyright and Licensing** — Copyright laws and code licensing must be followed where applicable." > "Do not distribute game files such as Assembly-CSharp.dll, unless given explicit permission by the game's developers." > "**Do not reupload packages or assets by other authors unless you have permission to redistribute them or are following their licensing.**" > "**Spam** — Packages that could be considered spam are not allowed. This includes (but is not limited to): ... **Packages that exist primarily to advertise an outside platform or service.**" That spam rule is directly relevant to a competing host: uploading a package to promote your hosting service is explicitly a removable offence. Also: https://wiki.thunderstore.io/llms-and-ai-generated-files — a page addressed to LLMs, stating *"If an LLM or other AI technology was used in the creation of a mod or Thunderstore package, it must be specified in the README.md file."* ## 3. Searches + GitHub — no terms anywhere All 404: `thunderstore.io/tos`, `/terms/`, `/legal/`, `/terms-of-service/`, and on `pages.thunderstore.io/p/`: `terms`, `terms-and-conditions`, `terms-of-use`, `tos`, `legal`, `eula`, `guidelines`, `rules`, `acceptable-use`, `dmca`, `copyright`, `content-policy`, `cookie-policy`, `about`, `impressum`. No CONTRIBUTING.md, no terms; `docs/` holds only `conventions.md`, `db-upgrade.md`, and two service-layer design docs. - Only **4 blog posts** exist at blog.thunderstore.io — none mention terms, API policy, or mirroring. - API schema self-describes as: `"Schema is automatically generated and not completely accurate."` Contact is a **Discord link**, not a legal address. Searching the full OpenAPI doc for `terms`, `rate limit`, `throttl`, `abuse`, `attribution`, `commercial`, `user-agent` → **all false**. Source comment (`robotsTxt.tsx`): *"Crawlers are kept out of the API and auth endpoints, but allowed into the API docs."* This binds crawlers by convention only; it is not a contract, and Thunderstore simultaneously documents the API publicly and ships first-party clients that hammer it. **The nearest thing to enforceable written terms Thunderstore has published** is the brand repo, https://github.com/thunderstore-io/brand-guidelines — and for a competing host this is the paragraph that actually matters: > "## Terms > - **Don't claim to be officially affiliated with the Thunderstore project unless explicitly given permission to do so.** > - **Don't use the assets for purposes which aren't related to the Thunderstore ecosystem.** > - If you're uncertain about your use case, ask and we'll clarify!" ## 4. Third-party mod managers **No statement blessing, tolerating, or restricting third-party clients exists** — NOT FOUND as an explicit policy. But the *conduct* evidence is strong and consistent, and it runs toward tolerance: - **Official API tokens are issued to third-party clients.** Gale's own docs walk users through generating one from Thunderstore's UI: *"Select a team and go to Service Accounts. Not to be confused with OAuth login process triggered from a browser."** - The bulk endpoints are explicitly designed for external consumers: `/api/experimental/package-index/` — *"Response is a stream of newline delimited JSON. Download links are not included in the response. The client is expected to build them using the following pattern: https://thunderstore.io/package/download/{namespace}/{name}/{version_number}/"* — and `/c/{community}/api/v1/package-listing-index/` supports `If-Modified-Since` for cached mirroring. **CORRECTION to your premise: r2modman was NOT acquired or absorbed by Thunderstore.** I could not verify that, and the primary sources contradict it: - `github.com/thunderstore-io/r2modmanPlus` is labelled on GitHub **"forked from ebkr/r2modmanPlus"** — a fork (4 stars, created 2022-06-27, still pushed 2026-09-07), not a transferred repo. - The canonical repo is still `ebkr/r2modmanPlus`, MIT, **"Copyright (c) 2020 Cade Ayres"** — ebkr's own copyright, unchanged. The `thunderstore2026` path segment plus DatHost's public affiliate program (30% of every referral payment for up to 24 months, per dathost.com/affiliate) indicate a **commercial referral/affiliate arrangement, not equity or exclusivity**. The code comment *"Adding another community is a one-line data change"* means it can expand to any game overnight. **Implication for your client:** Thunderstore monetizes game-server-hosting referrals directly, and its global rules ban *"Packages that exist primarily to advertise an outside platform or service."* A competing host advertising through packages is a rule violation; advertising through the sanctioned channel means buying into the same ad inventory (NitroPay/Overwolf slots, `nimbus-v2-*` containers) that DatHost currently occupies. --- ## Final answer to #6 **There is no formal, published, binding Thunderstore Terms of Service.** What exists instead is a fragmented set of non-contractual documents: | Document | URL | Status | |---|---|---| | Privacy Policy | pages.thunderstore.io/p/privacy-policy | Real, GDPR-only, references a ToS that isn't published | | Global Rules | wiki.thunderstore.io/moderation/global-rules | Moderation guidance, not a user contract | | Brand guidelines "Terms" | github.com/thunderstore-io/brand-guidelines | Nearest thing to enforceable terms; 3 bullet points | | robots.txt | thunderstore.io/robots.txt | `Disallow: /api/`; convention, not contract | | Software licenses | AGPL-3.0 (backend), MIT (r2modman) | Cover code only, not hosted data or packages | | **Terms of Service** | **does not exist** | **404 at every URL, zero hits in source** | **The smoking gun:** Thunderstore's login modal (`Navigation.tsx:500-504`) tells every user: > "**By logging in and accessing the site you agree to Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy**" …and the "Terms and Conditions" link resolves to `linkId="TermsOfService"` → `url={"/terms-of-service/"}` (`LinkLibrary.tsx:247`) → **`https://thunderstore.io/terms-of-service/` returns 404**, with no such route registered in `routes.ts`. The only restraint on record is `robots.txt`'s `Disallow: /api/`. - **No contractual hook** exists for Thunderstore to restrict a competing host's use of public API data. Their realistic levers are technical (Cloudflare/CDN blocking), the brand-guidelines affiliation rule, and the global rules if you upload packages.
